concepts.name: Collecting economic data: research techniques
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Primary and secondary data; interviews, questionnaires (open and closed questions, wording, piloting), surveys, observation, sampling (random, systematic, stratified, quota; sample size and bias) and experiments; the strengths and weaknesses of each technique, reliability and validity, and choosing a technique for an economic question. OUT: calculating averages and presenting data (aecon.tools.data-analysis).

concepts.name: Mean, mode and median, and presenting and analysing economic data
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Mean, mode and median from raw, frequency and grouped data (class mid-points), the weighted mean and which average suits which data; tables and schedules, pie charts (angles), bar charts, line graphs, frequency polygons and pictorial data, described in words and built from a table; reading, comparing and criticising data, simple percentages, percentage change and simple index numbers. OUT: the weighted CPI and real values (aecon.macro.price-indices-real-values).

concepts.name: Economics as a social science: positive and normative statements, ceteris paribus and time periods
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Economics as a social science that builds and tests models; positive statements (testable) against normative statements (value judgements); the meaning and use of ceteris paribus; assumptions and limits of models; why economists disagree; the short run, the long run and the very long run. OUT: scarcity and opportunity cost (aecon.basics.scarcity-choice).

concepts.name: Scarcity, choice, opportunity cost and the basic questions
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Wants and needs against limited resources; scarcity faced by individuals, firms and governments; the need to choose; opportunity cost as the next best alternative given up, with worked examples from tables; the questions of what, how and for whom to produce; economic goods against free goods. Zimbabwean examples (household budgets, the national budget). OUT: PPCs (aecon.basics.ppc) and how systems answer the questions (aecon.basics.economic-systems).

concepts.name: Factors of production
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Land (natural resources), labour, capital and enterprise; physical capital against human capital; renewable and non-renewable resources and their sustainable use (ZIMSEC detail); capital-intensive and labour-intensive production; mobility of factors. OUT: the rewards to the factors (aecon.distribution.factor-rewards); the entrepreneur (aecon.basics.entrepreneur-specialisation).

concepts.name: Enterprise, the entrepreneur, specialisation and the division of labour
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). The role of the entrepreneur (risk-bearing, organising the other factors, innovation); characteristics of a successful entrepreneur and recognising an opportunity (ZIMSEC detail: idea generation, a business proposal, licensing and registration as requirements for forming a business); specialisation and the division of labour with their advantages (output per worker, skills, time) and disadvantages (boredom, interdependence, job loss). OUT: forms of business organisation (aecon.enterprise.business-forms-ethics); international specialisation (aecon.trade.absolute-comparative).

concepts.name: Production possibility curves
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). What a PPC shows (maximum combinations of two goods or of consumer and capital goods); points on, inside and outside the curve; efficiency and unemployed resources; constant opportunity cost (a straight line) and increasing opportunity cost (concave to the origin), with decreasing opportunity cost as ZIMSEC detail; calculating opportunity cost from a schedule; causes and consequences of shifts (resources, technology, education); actual against potential output; limits of the model. OUT: the trading possibility curve (aecon.trade.absolute-comparative).

concepts.name: Economic systems: market, planned and mixed economies
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). How market, planned (command) and mixed economies answer what, how and for whom; features, strengths and weaknesses of each; the roles of the state and of private ownership; moving between systems; describing the Zimbabwean economic system in neutral, factual terms (ZIMSEC detail). OUT: the functions of price (aecon.market.price-mechanism); central planning in Zimbabwe (aecon.intervention.central-planning-zimbabwe).

concepts.name: Classifying goods: free, private, public, merit and demerit goods
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Free goods against economic (private) goods; rivalry and excludability; public goods (non-rival, non-excludable, the free-rider problem, why the market under-provides them); quasi-public goods; merit goods (under-consumption through imperfect information) and demerit goods (over-consumption); common resources and the over-use problem (ZIMSEC detail: common property). OUT: policies towards them (aecon.intervention.*); the market-failure framework (aecon.intervention.market-failure).

concepts.name: Sources of capital for a business
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Personal savings, retained profit, loans (banks, microfinance), shares, leasing, hire purchase, trade credit and grants; the procedure for acquiring capital (business plan, collateral, application); choosing a source by cost, risk, control and term. OUT: how banks create credit (aecon.money.*); stock-market detail.

concepts.name: Business organisations and business ethics
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Sole trader, partnership, cooperative, private limited and public limited company (and state-owned enterprise): ownership, liability, control, finance and continuity, and choosing a form to suit the setting; business ethics: Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu, accountability, social responsibility and environmental consciousness. OUT: growth by merger (aecon.firms.growth-integration).

concepts.name: Demand: the demand curve, its determinants and shifts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Effective demand (willingness and ability to pay); the law of demand and its reasons (income and substitution effects, diminishing marginal utility); individual and market demand (adding schedules); determinants (own price, income, prices of related goods, tastes, population, expectations); movements along against shifts of the curve; normal and inferior goods. OUT: elasticity (aecon.market.ped and following); utility theory (aecon.utility.*).

concepts.name: Supply: the supply curve, its determinants and shifts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). The law of supply; individual and market supply (adding schedules); determinants (costs of production, technology, indirect taxes and subsidies, prices of other goods, number of firms, weather, expectations); movements along against shifts of the curve. OUT: elasticity of supply (aecon.market.pes); cost curves (aecon.costs.*).

concepts.name: Price elasticity of demand: calculation, interpretation and determinants
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Definition and the formula % change in quantity demanded divided by % change in price, by the simple percentage-change method (base = original value; point and arc elasticity named as ZIMSEC checklist terms); meaning of the size and sign of the coefficient; perfectly elastic, highly elastic, unitary, highly inelastic and perfectly inelastic demand; factors affecting PED (substitutes, necessity, proportion of income, time, addiction). OUT: PED and revenue, and straight-line curves (aecon.market.ped-revenue).

concepts.name: PED, total revenue and decision-making
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). The link between PED and total expenditure/revenue for a price rise or fall; how PED varies along a straight-line demand curve (elastic at the top, unitary at the midpoint, inelastic at the bottom) with computed schedules; implications of PED for firms (pricing), households and government (indirect taxes, subsidies, agricultural prices). OUT: the basic calculation (aecon.market.ped); the kinked demand curve (aecon.firms.oligopoly).

concepts.name: Income elasticity and cross elasticity of demand
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Definitions, formulae and calculation of YED and XED; interpreting size and sign (normal, luxury and necessity goods, inferior goods; substitutes, complements and unrelated goods); factors affecting each; uses for firms (forecasting demand, product mix) and governments, including in developing economies. OUT: PED (aecon.market.ped).

concepts.name: Price elasticity of supply
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Definition, formula and calculation of PES; interpreting the coefficient; factors affecting it (spare capacity, stocks, time period, mobility of factors, perishability, ease of entry); momentary, short-run and long-run supply; how quickly and easily firms respond to changed conditions, with agricultural and mining examples. OUT: tax incidence (aecon.intervention.taxes-subsidies).

concepts.name: Market equilibrium and the effects of shifts in demand and supply
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Equilibrium and disequilibrium; excess demand and excess supply; how price adjusts; the effects on equilibrium price and quantity of shifts of either curve and of both together; solving linear schedules and equations; applications to primary products, foodstuffs, transport and foreign currency. OUT: consumer and producer surplus (aecon.market.surplus); price controls (aecon.intervention.price-controls-buffer-stocks).

concepts.name: Functions of the price mechanism and related markets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Prices as signals (transmission of preferences), rationing and incentives/rewards (ZIMSEC: signalling, rationing, rewarding); how a change in one market spreads to others: joint demand (complements), alternative demand (substitutes), derived demand and joint supply, with worked chains. OUT: comparing economic systems (aecon.basics.economic-systems).

concepts.name: Consumer surplus and producer surplus
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Meaning and significance of consumer surplus and producer surplus; measuring them as areas on linear curves (computed); how price changes, taxes, subsidies and price controls change them; the effect of PED and PES on the size of the changes. OUT: the welfare-loss triangle of externalities (aecon.intervention.externalities); Pareto efficiency (aecon.firms.efficiency).

concepts.name: Utility, diminishing marginal utility and the equi-marginal principle
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Total and marginal utility and their calculation from schedules; diminishing marginal utility; the equi-marginal principle (consumer equilibrium where MU/price is equal across goods) with computed examples; deriving an individual demand curve; limitations of the theory and its rationality assumptions. OUT: indifference curves (aecon.utility.indifference-curves).

concepts.name: Indifference curves, budget lines and the income, substitution and price effects
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Indifference curves (shape, slope, the marginal rate of substitution) and budget lines (slope = price ratio, shifts and pivots); consumer equilibrium; the income, substitution and price effects of a price change for normal, inferior and Giffen goods (decomposition done in words and numbers); limitations of the model. OUT: marginal utility (aecon.utility.marginal-utility).

concepts.name: Short-run production: fixed and variable factors and diminishing returns
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Short run against long run; fixed and variable factors; total, average and marginal product with calculations from schedules; the law of diminishing returns (variable proportions) and the relation between average and marginal product; productivity and why it matters for costs. OUT: costs (aecon.costs.short-run-costs).

concepts.name: Short-run costs: total, average and marginal
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). TFC, TVC, TC, AFC, AVC, ATC and MC defined and calculated from a schedule; the shapes of the short-run average and marginal cost curves and why (spreading fixed costs, diminishing returns); why MC cuts AVC and ATC at their minimum points. OUT: long-run costs (aecon.costs.long-run-costs-scale).

concepts.name: Long-run costs, returns to scale and economies and diseconomies of scale
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). No fixed factors in the long run; increasing, constant and decreasing returns to scale; the shape of the long-run average cost curve and minimum efficient scale; internal economies of scale (technical, managerial, financial, marketing, purchasing, risk-bearing) and external economies; internal and external diseconomies; the link between economies of scale and falling average cost. OUT: growth of firms (aecon.firms.growth-integration).

concepts.name: Revenue and the profit-maximising output
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Total, average and marginal revenue defined and calculated; revenue curves for a price-taker (horizontal) and for a firm facing a downward-sloping demand curve (MR below AR; MR zero at maximum TR); the profit-maximising output where MC = MR (with MC rising), found from schedules; applying demand and supply analysis to the firm. OUT: types of profit (aecon.costs.profit-types); behaviour in each market structure (aecon.firms.*).

concepts.name: Normal, subnormal and supernormal profit, losses and the shutdown decision
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Normal profit as the opportunity cost of enterprise (included in costs); supernormal (abnormal) and subnormal profit and loss; calculating profit as (AR - ATC) x Q from schedules; cost minimisation against profit maximisation (ZIMSEC detail); the short-run shutdown condition (price below AVC) and the long-run condition. OUT: market-structure detail (aecon.firms.*).

concepts.name: Objectives of firms
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Profit maximisation, survival, growth, sales (revenue) maximisation and profit satisficing; other objectives (social and ethical); why objectives differ and the effect on price and output; the principal-agent problem from the separation of ownership and control (Cambridge detail). OUT: pricing policies (aecon.firms.price-discrimination, aecon.firms.oligopoly).

concepts.name: Market structures: features, barriers to entry and contestable markets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). The spectrum from perfect competition to monopoly; number of buyers and sellers, product differentiation, freedom of entry and information; perfect competition, monopoly, natural monopoly, monopolistic competition and oligopoly compared; barriers to entry and exit (legal, market, cost, physical); contestable markets (features, sunk costs, implications for behaviour). OUT: the behaviour and outcomes in each structure (aecon.firms.perfect-competition and following).

concepts.name: Perfect competition
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Assumptions; the firm as a price-taker and its revenue curves; short-run equilibrium (profit or loss), long-run equilibrium with normal profit; the firm's supply curve (MC above AVC) and the shutdown price; efficiency of the long-run outcome; agricultural markets as approximations. OUT: monopoly (aecon.firms.monopoly).

concepts.name: Monopoly and natural monopoly
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Sources of monopoly power; revenue and equilibrium at MC = MR with supernormal profit and price above MC; comparison with perfect competition; welfare loss and X-inefficiency; benefits (economies of scale, innovation); natural monopoly and how it may be regulated. OUT: price discrimination (aecon.firms.price-discrimination).

concepts.name: Monopolistic competition
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Features (many firms, differentiated products, easy entry); non-price competition and advertising; short-run supernormal profit or loss and long-run normal profit (tangency solution described and computed); excess capacity and efficiency; local examples (salons, restaurants, retail).

concepts.name: Oligopoly: interdependence, concentration and pricing behaviour
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Features and interdependence; calculating concentration ratios; the kinked demand curve and price rigidity (revenue and MR gap); price competition and non-price competition; price leadership, limit pricing and predatory pricing; efficiency of oligopoly. OUT: collusion and game theory (aecon.firms.collusion-game-theory).

concepts.name: Collusion, cartels and the Prisoner's Dilemma
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Overt and tacit collusion; cartels (conditions for an effective cartel, the incentive to cheat, consequences; the only part the ZIMSEC checklist names); game theory with two-player pay-off matrices, dominant strategies and the Nash equilibrium, and the Prisoner's Dilemma and why collusion breaks down (Cambridge detail); competition law in outline. OUT: other oligopoly pricing (aecon.firms.oligopoly).

concepts.name: Price discrimination
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). First-, second- and third-degree price discrimination; the conditions for it (market power, separable markets, different PED); effects on revenue, consumers and efficiency; numerical example with two markets (MR = MC in each); examples such as transport, electricity tariffs and student fares.

concepts.name: Economic efficiency: productive, allocative, technical, dynamic and X-efficiency
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Definitions and conditions: productive efficiency (lowest point of ATC), allocative efficiency (P = MC), technical efficiency (ZIMSEC detail), Pareto optimality, dynamic efficiency and X-inefficiency; comparing the efficiency, advantages and disadvantages of the market structures and evaluating them for an economy (ZIMSEC detail). OUT: market failure causes (aecon.intervention.market-failure).

concepts.name: Growth of firms: organic growth, mergers and takeovers
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Reasons for different sizes of firm; organic growth and diversification; external growth by merger or takeover: horizontal, vertical (forward and backward) and conglomerate integration, reasons and consequences for firms, consumers and workers. OUT: multinational companies (aecon.dev.mncs-fdi); small firms (aecon.firms.sme).

concepts.name: Small and medium enterprises
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). Definition of small and medium enterprises (criteria vary by country; none assumed); why small firms survive (niche markets, personal service, flexibility, low barriers); their problems (finance, markets, infrastructure, regulation); government involvement and support; benefits of SMEs to society including employment and the move from informal to formal activity, described factually and neutrally. OUT: large firms (aecon.firms.growth-integration).

concepts.name: Rewards to the factors of production
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Rent, wages, interest and profit as the rewards to land, labour, capital and enterprise; what determines each at an introductory level (demand for and supply of the factor); functional against personal income distribution; why rewards differ. OUT: economic rent (aecon.distribution.rent-transfer-earnings); MRP theory (aecon.labour.demand-mrp).

concepts.name: Economic rent, transfer earnings and quasi-rent
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Transfer earnings as the minimum payment needed to keep a factor in its current use (its opportunity cost); economic rent as the surplus over transfer earnings; how supply elasticity decides the split (perfectly inelastic supply: all rent), with computed examples; factors affecting rent and transfer earnings in an occupation; quasi-rent as a short-run surplus on a fixed asset (ZIMSEC detail).

concepts.name: Demand for labour and marginal revenue product theory
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge A Level only). Labour demand as a derived demand; marginal physical product and marginal revenue product (MRP = MPP x MR) calculated from schedules; the firm hires until the MRP equals the marginal cost of labour; factors changing the demand for labour in a firm or occupation; applying MRP theory to land and capital (ZIMSEC detail). OUT: supply of labour (aecon.labour.supply).

concepts.name: Supply of labour and of the other factors
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge A Level only). Supply of labour to a firm and to an occupation: wage and non-wage factors (hours, conditions, training, status); movements along against shifts; labour mobility (geographical and occupational); the determinants of the supply of land and capital (ZIMSEC detail). OUT: wage determination (aecon.labour.wage-determination).

concepts.name: Wage determination in perfect and imperfect labour markets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge A Level only). Equilibrium wage and employment in a competitive market; the influence of trade unions, a national minimum wage and monopsony employers on wages and employment, with schedules; labour-market imperfections and wages legislation (ZIMSEC detail). OUT: wage differentials (aecon.labour.wage-differentials).

concepts.name: Wage differentials
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Differences between occupations explained by labour-market forces (skill, training, productivity, risk, compensating differences, demand and supply) and by non-economic factors (discrimination, bargaining power, tradition); mobility and differentials; evaluating the reasons in a developing economy such as Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Market failure and the reasons for government intervention
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Market failure as a misallocation of resources; its sources: public goods, externalities, merit and demerit goods, imperfect and asymmetric information, moral hazard, monopoly power, factor immobility, common property and inequality; reasons for intervening in individual markets, including volatile prices of primary products. OUT: the definitions of types of good (aecon.basics.goods-classification); the externality model (aecon.intervention.externalities); the policies (the other aecon.intervention.* concepts).

concepts.name: Externalities, social costs and benefits and welfare loss
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Private, external and social costs and benefits (SC = PC + EC; the marginal versions MSC, MPC, MEC, MSB, MPB, MEB) with calculations; positive and negative externalities of consumption and production; the deadweight welfare loss from over- or under-provision, computed from linear curves. OUT: cost-benefit analysis (aecon.intervention.cost-benefit); policies (aecon.intervention.*).

concepts.name: Indirect taxes and subsidies: impact and incidence
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Specific and ad valorem indirect taxes; the effect on supply, price and quantity; incidence on consumers and producers and the role of PED and PES, computed; tax revenue; subsidies, their cost and incidence; using taxes and subsidies to correct externalities and their effectiveness. OUT: the taxes of fiscal policy (aecon.policy.taxes).

concepts.name: Maximum and minimum prices and buffer stock schemes
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Maximum prices below the equilibrium (shortages, rationing, black markets) and minimum prices above it (surpluses; minimum farm prices and minimum wages); how a buffer stock scheme buys when prices are low and sells when high, its costs and problems; marketing arrangements for grain as a factual example; effects on consumers, producers and the government budget.

concepts.name: Direct provision of goods and services and provision of information
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Direct provision by government (education, health, roads) for public and merit goods, financing and efficiency problems; provision of information (labelling, campaigns, health warnings) to correct imperfect information, and its limits. OUT: nudges and regulation (aecon.intervention.regulation-permits-nudge).

concepts.name: Regulation, quotas, licences, pollution permits, property rights and nudges
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Regulation and deregulation; production quotas; prohibitions and licences; tradable pollution permits; property rights as a way to internalise externalities; behavioural insights and nudge theory (defaults, framing); strengths and weaknesses of each. OUT: taxes and subsidies (aecon.intervention.taxes-subsidies); nationalisation and privatisation (aecon.intervention.privatisation).

concepts.name: Nationalisation, privatisation and commercialisation
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Nationalisation, privatisation and the commercialisation of state enterprises (ZIMSEC detail); reasons for each; effects on efficiency, equity, revenue and employment; regulation after privatisation; state enterprise reform described factually and neutrally.

concepts.name: Government failure and evaluating microeconomic intervention
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Definition of government failure; its causes (poor information, regulatory capture, unintended consequences, administrative cost, short-term political horizons) and consequences; the strengths and weaknesses of each solution to market failure (ZIMSEC detail) and evaluating intervention in an economy such as Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Cost-benefit analysis
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). The principle of cost-benefit analysis: identifying private and social costs and benefits, valuing intangibles, discounting future values (net present value is not required by Cambridge), the decision rule; a worked example for a fictional road, dam or clinic; limitations and its role in decision-making.

concepts.name: Central planning and decision-making in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). How central planners allocate resources; strengths and weaknesses of central planning; the decision-making process in Zimbabwe described factually and neutrally (budget cycle, national development plans); a reviewer must check the institutional detail. OUT: other economic systems (aecon.basics.economic-systems).

concepts.name: Wages legislation, incomes policy and land reform as interventions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). Wages legislation and minimum wages, collective bargaining and incomes policy, controls on trade unions, and the land reform programme treated as examples of intervention in factor markets, assessed on efficiency, equity and output with balanced, factual and politically neutral treatment (ZIMSEC detail). OUT: general wage theory (aecon.labour.wage-determination).

concepts.name: Income and wealth inequality and redistribution policies
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Income as a flow and wealth as a stock; measuring inequality with the Gini coefficient (calculation not required at AS); economic reasons for inequality; policies to redistribute income and wealth: minimum wage, transfer payments, progressive income taxes, inheritance and capital taxes, state provision of essential goods; effectiveness. OUT: Lorenz curve construction (aecon.dev.income-distribution-lorenz).

concepts.name: Equity, equality, efficiency, poverty and the poverty trap
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). The difference between equity and equality and between equity and efficiency; absolute and relative poverty; the poverty trap; policies such as negative income tax, universal and means-tested benefits and universal basic income, and their evaluation.

concepts.name: Measuring national income: GDP, GNI/GNP, NNI and per capita income
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Meaning of national income; the output, income and expenditure approaches (ZIMSEC detail); GDP, GNI (GNP), NNI/NNP and per capita measures; adjustments from market to basic prices and from gross to net values; calculations; limitations of the statistics (informal economy, non-marketed output). OUT: real values and price indices (aecon.macro.price-indices-real-values).

concepts.name: Price indices, the GDP deflator and real against nominal values
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Constructing a weighted consumer price index (base year, basket, weights) and the retail price index; difficulties in measurement; the inflation rate; nominal against real values; the GDP deflator and real GDP; converting nominal to real figures and the use for comparing living standards over time. OUT: causes of inflation (aecon.macro.inflation).

concepts.name: The circular flow of income
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Flows between households, firms, government and the international sector in closed and open economies; injections and leakages; equilibrium and disequilibrium in the flow; reading and describing a flow diagram. OUT: the multiplier (aecon.macro.multiplier).

concepts.name: Aggregate demand
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Definition; AD = C + I + G + (X - M) and the meaning of each component; determinants; why the AD curve slopes downward; causes of a shift of AD; movement along against shift. OUT: consumption and investment functions (aecon.macro.consumption-saving-investment).

concepts.name: Aggregate supply: short-run and long-run
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Definition and determinants of aggregate supply; the shape of SRAS (upward-sloping line or sweeping curve) and of LRAS (vertical, or in three sections: highly elastic, upward-sloping, vertical); causes of shifts in SRAS and LRAS; movement against shift.

concepts.name: AD/AS equilibrium: output, the price level and employment
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Establishing equilibrium real output, price level and employment; the effects of shifts of AD and of AS (demand-pull, cost-push, supply shocks, growth) on those variables, shown in worked schedules and described diagrams. OUT: gaps and the multiplier (aecon.macro.income-gaps).

concepts.name: Economic growth: meaning, measurement, causes and consequences
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Meaning of economic growth and its distinction from development; measuring growth (real GDP, real GDP per head; nominal against real growth rates); causes (factor quantity and quality, productivity, investment, technology, institutions); consequences for living standards, the environment, inequality and inflation. OUT: output gaps and cycles (aecon.macro.growth-cycles-gaps).

concepts.name: Actual and potential growth, output gaps and the trade cycle
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Actual against potential growth; positive and negative output gaps; the business (trade) cycle, its phases and causes; automatic stabilisers; policies to promote growth and their effectiveness.

concepts.name: Inclusive and sustainable economic growth
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Inclusive growth: meaning, the effect of growth on equity and equality, policies; sustainable growth: using and conserving resources, the effect of growth on the environment and climate change, policies to mitigate it (taxes, regulation, investment in renewable energy); Zimbabwean examples (mining, energy, land) factual and neutral.

concepts.name: Unemployment: measurement, types, causes and consequences
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Meaning of unemployment; labour-force and unemployment-rate calculations; difficulties in measuring (hidden unemployment, informal work, underemployment); frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal and technological unemployment; consequences for individuals, firms, government and the economy. OUT: the natural rate and policies (aecon.macro.unemployment-natural-rate).

concepts.name: Equilibrium and disequilibrium unemployment, the natural rate, mobility and policies
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Full employment; equilibrium and disequilibrium unemployment including hysteresis; voluntary and involuntary unemployment; the natural rate of unemployment (definition, determinants, policy implications); patterns and trends; geographical and occupational mobility of labour; policies to reduce unemployment and their effectiveness.

concepts.name: Inflation, deflation and disinflation: causes, consequences and control
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Definitions of inflation, deflation and disinflation; demand-pull and cost-push inflation; consequences (redistribution, menu and shoe-leather costs, uncertainty, competitiveness, hyperinflation described factually); policies to reduce inflation (monetary, fiscal, supply-side, wage and price controls) and their effectiveness. OUT: index construction (aecon.macro.price-indices-real-values); the quantity theory (aecon.money.quantity-theory).

concepts.name: Consumption, saving and investment functions
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Autonomous and induced consumption, C = a + bY; average and marginal propensities to consume, save, import and tax (calculated); the savings function; autonomous and induced investment, its determinants and the accelerator; government spending and net exports as components of AD. OUT: the multiplier (aecon.macro.multiplier).

concepts.name: The multiplier
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Definition of the multiplier; formulae and calculation in a closed and an open economy, with and without a government sector (k = 1/(MPS + MRT + MPM) and the simpler forms); calculating the effect of a change in injections or AD on national income; time lags and limitations. OUT: inflationary and deflationary gaps (aecon.macro.income-gaps).

concepts.name: National income determination and inflationary and deflationary gaps
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Equilibrium national income from AD and the income approach; the full employment level of income; inflationary and deflationary gaps defined and calculated with the multiplier; policy implications.

concepts.name: Keynesian and monetarist schools of thought
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). The main differences between Keynesian and monetarist (classical) views on the role of money, wage and price flexibility, the shape of aggregate supply, unemployment and the role of government; policy implications; evaluating both (ZIMSEC detail).

concepts.name: Macroeconomic policy objectives
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Price stability, low unemployment/full employment, economic growth and development, balance of payments stability, equity and sustainability as objectives; how success is measured; targets. OUT: conflicts between objectives (aecon.policy.interrelated-problems-phillips).

concepts.name: Taxation: types, rates and reasons
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Direct and indirect taxes; progressive, regressive and proportional taxes; average and marginal rates of tax with banded calculations; reasons for taxation; canons of taxation (ZIMSEC checklist). OUT: incidence of indirect taxes (aecon.intervention.taxes-subsidies); the Laffer curve (aecon.policy.effectiveness-conflicts).

concepts.name: Fiscal policy: the budget, national debt and expansionary and contractionary policy
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). The government budget, deficit and surplus; the national debt and its significance; types of and reasons for government spending (capital and current); expansionary and contractionary fiscal policy; AD/AS analysis of their effects on output, prices and employment; the Zimbabwean budget as a factual illustration. OUT: taxes (aecon.policy.taxes).

concepts.name: Monetary policy
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Definition; tools: interest rates, money supply (open-market operations, reserve requirements) and credit regulations; expansionary and contractionary monetary policy; AD/AS analysis of the effects; the transmission mechanism and its limits. OUT: credit creation arithmetic (aecon.money.credit-creation).

concepts.name: Supply-side policy
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Meaning in terms of the effect on LRAS; objectives (productivity and productive capacity); tools such as training, infrastructure, support for technology, tax incentives and deregulation; AD/AS analysis of the effects on output, prices and employment; time lags. OUT: market-based against interventionist evaluation (aecon.policy.effectiveness-conflicts).

concepts.name: Links between macroeconomic problems and the Phillips curve
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). The internal and external value of money; relationships between the balance of payments and inflation, growth and inflation, and growth and the balance of payments; the inflation-unemployment trade-off: traditional Phillips curve, the expectations-augmented short-run and long-run Phillips curves and the natural rate; stagflation; conflicts between objectives such as price stability against unemployment (ZIMSEC detail).

concepts.name: Effectiveness of macroeconomic policies, policy conflicts and government failure
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Effectiveness of fiscal policy (including Laffer curve analysis), monetary policy, supply-side policy (market-based and interventionist), exchange rate policy and international trade policy against each objective; problems and conflicts from the outcomes; government failure in macroeconomic policy (time lags, crowding out, poor forecasts); evaluating policy for the Zimbabwean economy (ZIMSEC detail).

concepts.name: Money: functions and characteristics
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Barter and its problems; the functions (medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, standard of deferred payment) and characteristics (acceptability, durability, portability, divisibility, uniformity, limited supply, stability) of money; forms of money (commodity, notes and coins, bank deposits, electronic and mobile money); effect of inflation on money's functions.

concepts.name: Banks and the central bank: functions and objectives
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Money market institutions: commercial banks, building societies, merchant banks and the central bank (ZIMSEC); functions of commercial banks (deposit accounts, overdrafts and loans, balance sheet assets and liabilities), reserve and capital ratios, and the objectives of liquidity, security and profitability and their conflict; roles of the central bank (banker to the government and to banks, lender of last resort, note issue, implementing monetary policy, supervision). OUT: credit-creation arithmetic (aecon.money.credit-creation).

concepts.name: Credit creation and the bank credit multiplier
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Fractional reserve banking; how an initial deposit supports a larger volume of deposits; the credit (money) multiplier 1/reserve ratio with step-by-step computed tables; the limits to credit creation (cash drain, excess reserves, loan demand); the effect on the money supply.

concepts.name: The money supply and the demand for money
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Definition and measures of the money supply (narrow and broad); causes of changes in the money supply in an open economy: credit creation, the central bank, government deficit financing, quantitative easing and the balance of payments; determinants of the demand for money (transactions, precautionary and speculative motives). OUT: interest-rate theories (aecon.money.interest-rates); the quantity theory (aecon.money.quantity-theory).

concepts.name: The quantity theory of money
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). The equation of exchange MV = PT; the assumptions (V and T constant in the short run); calculations; the link between the money supply and the price level (ZIMSEC detail); monetarist conclusions about inflation; criticisms.

concepts.name: Interest rate determination: liquidity preference, loanable funds and non-economic factors
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). The liquidity preference theory (demand for money, fixed money supply); the loanable funds theory (savings and investment demand); the Keynesian view; real against nominal interest rates; other determinants (risk, term, inflation expectations, central bank rate, non-economic factors in ZIMSEC); applying the theories to an economy.

concepts.name: Absolute and comparative advantage
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Definitions; calculating opportunity costs from output tables for two countries and two goods; the gains from specialisation and the range of terms of trade; the trading possibility curve; limitations and assumptions of the theories (transport costs, constant costs, mobility, changing advantage); Zimbabwe's advantages stated generally. OUT: terms of trade measures (aecon.trade.terms-of-trade).

concepts.name: The case for and against free trade
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Determinants of trade flows (comparative advantage, exchange rates, incomes, political factors); benefits of specialisation and free trade (efficiency, choice, scale, competition, growth) and its costs (adjustment unemployment, dependence, dumping, structural change); justifying free trade. OUT: protectionism (aecon.trade.protectionism).

concepts.name: Protectionism: tools, impacts and arguments
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Tariffs (effect on price, quantity, revenue and welfare, computed), import quotas, export subsidies, embargoes and administrative barriers; arguments for protection (infant industries, strategic industries, dumping, balance of payments, employment) and against it (inefficiency, higher prices, retaliation); evaluating protectionism for developing countries.

concepts.name: Economic integration: trading blocs, trade creation and diversion, and trade agreements
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Free trade area, customs union, monetary union and full economic union (and common market as a step); trade creation and trade diversion; merits and demerits; regional examples such as SADC and COMESA (described cautiously); commodity agreements, GATT/WTO and bilateral agreements (ZIMSEC detail).

concepts.name: Terms of trade
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Terms of trade = export price index / import price index x 100, calculated; causes of changes (exchange rate, relative prices, commodity prices, productivity, demand); the impact of improvement and deterioration on the balance of payments and living standards; primary-commodity exporters.

concepts.name: The current account of the balance of payments
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Components: trade in goods, trade in services, primary income and secondary income; calculating the balance of trade in goods, in services, in goods and services, and the current account balance; surplus and deficit; causes of imbalances and their consequences for the domestic and external economy. OUT: the capital and financial accounts (aecon.trade.bop-accounts).

concepts.name: The full balance of payments: current, capital and financial accounts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). The structure of the accounts: current account, capital account and financial account (direct, portfolio and other investment, reserves/official financing in ZIMSEC: balance for official financing); the balancing item and why the accounts balance; surplus and deficit as disequilibrium; calculations.

concepts.name: Policies to correct balance of payments imbalances
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). The objective of current account stability; effects of fiscal, monetary, supply-side, protectionist and exchange rate policies; expenditure-switching against expenditure-reducing policies; ZIMSEC trade policies (exchange rate policy, import substitution, protectionism, export promotion and the 'Look East' policy described factually); evaluation.

concepts.name: Exchange rates: determination of a floating rate
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Definition of an exchange rate; demand for and supply of a currency; appreciation and depreciation; causes of changes (relative interest rates and inflation, trade flows, investment, speculation); converting currencies and percentage changes, computed. OUT: fixed and managed systems (aecon.trade.exchange-rate-systems).

concepts.name: Fixed, managed and floating exchange rate systems
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Fixed (pegged), managed floating and floating systems; determination under fixed and managed systems; revaluation and devaluation; intervention and reserves; nominal against real and trade-weighted exchange rates (index calculations); strengths and weaknesses; the use of foreign currencies alongside a local currency described neutrally.

concepts.name: Effects of exchange rate changes: AD/AS, Marshall-Lerner and the J-curve
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). How appreciation and depreciation change export and import prices, AD (net exports), SRAS (imported inputs), output, prices and employment; the Marshall-Lerner condition (sum of the two price elasticities greater than 1) and the J-curve; exchange rate policy (ZIMSEC) and competitiveness.

concepts.name: Measuring living standards and economic development
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Classifying economies by development and by income; real per capita national income (GDP, GNI, NNI) and purchasing power parity; problems of comparison using money measures; non-monetary indicators; composite indicators (HDI, MEW, MPI); the Kuznets curve; comparing growth rates and living standards over time and between countries (ZIMSEC: comparison of living standards).

concepts.name: Population: birth, death, migration and structure
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Measurement and causes of changes in the birth rate, death rate, infant mortality and net migration; natural increase and population change; the age structure and dependency ratio; optimum population; urbanisation; Zimbabwean context stated generally (HIV/AIDS, migration, remittances), with no invented statistics.

concepts.name: Economic structure and characteristics of developing and developed countries
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Employment composition by primary, secondary and tertiary sector; the pattern of trade (primary against manufactured goods); dependence on a few commodities; infrastructure, informal sector, saving and investment, technology; comparing the characteristics of developing and developed countries (ZIMSEC detail).

concepts.name: Income distribution: the Lorenz curve and the Gini coefficient
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Cumulative income and population shares; describing and interpreting a Lorenz curve; calculating the Gini coefficient from cumulative shares; comparing distributions over time and between countries; limitations. OUT: policies on inequality (aecon.equity.*).

concepts.name: International aid, external debt, the IMF and the World Bank
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Forms of aid (grants, loans, bilateral, multilateral, tied, technical, emergency), reasons for giving it, its effects and importance; trade and investment links; causes and consequences of external debt and debt service; the roles of the IMF and the World Bank, described neutrally.

concepts.name: Multinational companies and foreign direct investment
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Definition and activities of multinational companies; foreign direct investment, its definition and reasons; benefits (capital, technology, jobs, tax revenue) and costs (profit repatriation, dependence, environment) for host economies; multinationals as large firms (ZIMSEC) and local-ownership policies described factually.

concepts.name: Globalisation: meaning, causes and consequences
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Meaning of globalisation; causes (technology, lower transport and communication costs, trade liberalisation, capital mobility, multinational companies); consequences for economies, workers, the environment and developing countries; assessing gains and losses.

concepts.name: Using diagrams, data and calculations in economics answers
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge AS and A Level). Describing and labelling diagrams in words (axes, curves, equilibrium, shifts); what examiners reward in a diagram; reading tables and graphs, selecting evidence from source material, percentage change and index calculations; using units and rounding; how data-response questions are structured (ZIMSEC Paper 2, Cambridge Section A). OUT: essay writing (aecon.skills.essay-evaluation).

concepts.name: Writing economics essays: analysis and evaluation
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Forms 5-6; Cambridge AS and A Level). Command words (define, explain, analyse, assess, discuss, evaluate); building chains of reasoning; evaluation (short run against long run, size of effects, elasticity, assumptions, context, priorities and value judgements) and a justified conclusion; planning, timing and structure for ZIMSEC Paper 3 essays and Cambridge Section B/C essays; levels-based marking.
